chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Hamdan ibn Suleyman, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sallam, from Ahmad ibn Bakr ibn Isam, from Dawood al-Raqqi, who said:

I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), and I had some wealth upon a man, and I feared it would be lost. So I complained to him about that. He said to me: 'When you go to Makkah, perform a Tawaf on behalf of Abdul Muttalib and pray two Rak'ahs on his behalf, and perform a Tawaf on behalf of Abu Talib and pray two Rak'ahs on his behalf, and perform a Tawaf on behalf of Abdullah and pray two Rak'ahs on his behalf, and perform a Tawaf on behalf of Amina and pray two Rak'ahs on her behalf, and perform a Tawaf on behalf of Fatima bint Asad and pray two Rak'ahs on her behalf. Then supplicate that your wealth be returned to you.'
He said: 'So I did that. Then I went out from the Door of Al-Safa, and there was my debtor standing there saying, 'O Dawood! You withheld me for long. Come, take possession of your wealth'.'

key_terms.فَاطِمَةُ بِنْتُ أَسَدٍ: Fatima bint Asad (mother of Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What ritual acts did Imam al-Sadiq recommend for recovering lost wealth or debts?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Shia practice of *Tawaf al-Nawafil* (voluntary circumambulation) performed on behalf of the deceased, specifically highlighting the intercessory merit of the Prophet’s immediate family. The narrative underscores the spiritual efficacy of combining ritual devotion with supplication (*dua*) to resolve worldly concerns, as evidenced by the immediate recovery of Dawood al-Raqqi’s debt. It reflects the broader theological belief in the continued influence of the Ahl al-Bayt in the spiritual and material realms.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Hamdan Bin Suleyman, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Bin Sallam, from Ahmad Bin Bakr Bin Isam, from Dawood Al Raqqy who said,

‘I went over to Abu Abdullahasws, and there was some wealth for me upon a man, and I had feared losing it. So I complained to himasws, and heasws said to me: ‘When you go to Makkah, perform Tawaaf on behalf of Abdul Muttalibas with one Tawaaf, and Pray two Cycles of Salaat on hisas behalf, and perform Tawaaf on behalf of Abu Talibas with a Tawaar, and Pray on hisas behalf two Cycles of Salaat, and perform Tawaaf on behalf of Abdullahas with a Tawaaf and Pray on hisas behalf two Cycles of Salaat, and perform Tawaaf on behalf of Aaminaas with a Tawaaf, and Pray on heras behalf two Cycles of Salaat, and perform Tawaaf on behalf of Fatimaasws Bin Asadasws with a Tawaaf, and Pray on her behalf two Cycles of Prayer. The supplicate for the return of your wealth to you’.
He (the narrator) said, ‘So I did that. Then I went out from the Door of Al-Safa, and there was my debtor pausing there saying, ‘O Dawood! You withheld me for long. Take possession of your wealth’.
en.sarwar: 21. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Sulayman from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad ibn Salam from Ahmad ibn Bakr ibn ‘Isam from Dawud al-Riqqiy who has said the following:

“I once went to see abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam. A man owed me a certain amount of money and I was afraid of losing it. I complained before him about it. He said, ‘When you go to Makkah you should perform Tawaf on behalf of ‘Abd al-Muttalib, then you should perform two Rak‘at salat (prayer), and then perform Tawaf on behalf of abu Talib and two Rak‘at salat (prayer). You then should perform Tawaf on behalf of ‘Abd Allah, then two Rak‘at salat (prayer), perform Tawaf on behalf of Aminah, then two Rak‘at salat (prayer), perform Tawaf on behalf of Fatimah bint Asad, then two Rak‘at salat (prayer). Then pray for the return of your money.’

He (the narrator) has said, ‘I followed the instruction. Then I was leaving through the door of al-Safa’ and I saw my borrower standing, who said, ‘O Dawud, you kept me here for so long. Come and get your money.’”
